claims.text: A tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy can serve as an effective interlayer between W and CuCrZr.
An interlayer with an intermediate coefficient of thermal expansion would reduce thermal stresses between W and CuCrZr.
Enhanced chemical inertness of the interlayer would limit interfacial interdiffusion.
Directly joined W and CuCrZr suffer from a large thermal-expansion mismatch.
Directly joined W and CuCrZr undergo unwanted chemical interactions that cause interfacial instability under extreme conditions.
A tungsten-based RHEA can contain refractory alloying elements such as Ta, Nb, and Mo.
Tuning the Ta, Nb, or Mo content can produce an intermediate thermal-expansion coefficient and improved chemical stability for the W/CuCrZr interface.
Magnetron sputtering followed by annealing is an appropriate route for producing the proposed RHEA interlayer.
Fusion-reactor components face high temperatures, large heat loads, and neutron exposure.
The proposed joint will face rapid thermal cycling in service.
Controlled high-temperature post-annealing forms a nanocrystalline RHEA interlayer.
The post-annealed interlayer has a coherent microstructure.
A nanocrystalline, coherent interlayer mitigates strain accumulation and suppresses interfacial interdiffusion.
The RHEA interlayer provides a graded transition in thermal-expansion behavior and chemical compatibility between W and CuCrZr.
The graded transition reduces stress concentrations and interfacial reactions during high-temperature operation and irradiation.
The RHEA interlayer will improve interfacial bonding and the mechanical stability and longevity of W/CuCrZr components.
Direct W-to-CuCrZr bonding typically undergoes reaction-induced degradation under high-temperature irradiation conditions.
Interlayer performance depends on precise control of RHEA composition and post-deposition annealing.
Loss of interlayer microstructural stability during prolonged irradiation or thermal cycling would diminish its interfacial benefits.
The optimal alloying elements, concentrations, and long-term neutron-irradiation stability remain experimentally unvalidated.
